knowledge:
- key_parameters: lborder=integer defining the upstream boundary for peak annotation ;; rborder=integer defining the downstream boundary for peak annotation ;; method=character string specifying the peak annotation aggregation method (e.g. "sum") ;; network=a regulon object containing the gene regulatory network ;; contrast=character vector of length 2 specifying the conditions to compare ;; minsize=minimum number of genes in a regulon to perform the analysis ;; method in gsea=method for GSEA p-value estimation (e.g. "pareto")
- alternatives: The VIPER package can be used directly for gene expression data, but vulcan is preferred when analyzing promoter-level differential binding signatures from ChIP-Seq data.
- when_to_use: Use when you have ChIP-Seq data (BAM and BED files) for a transcription factor under different conditions and want to identify candidate co-regulators using a gene regulatory network (e.g. ARACNe network).
- pitfalls: When working with small or reduced datasets (such as single-chromosome examples), the default minimum regulon size might be too large, resulting in no hits; in these cases, the minsize parameter must be manually reduced (e.g. minsize=5).

workflows.name: vulcan_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the full VULCAN pipeline to identify co-regulatory factors from ChIP-Seq data and a regulatory network.
input: vfile.csv (annotation sheet pointing to BAM and BED files)
workflows.stages: 1. Import ChIP-Seq data using vulcan.import ;; 2. Annotate peaks to gene names using vulcan.annotate ;; 3. Normalize peak abundance using vulcan.normalize ;; 4. Run VULCAN analysis using vulcan ;; 5. Plot master regulators using plot
workflows.code:
vfile<-tempfile()
vulcandata::vulcansheet(vfile)
vobj<-vulcandata::vulcanexample()
unlink(vfile)
vobj<-vulcan.annotate(vobj,lborder=-10000,rborder=10000,method="sum")
vobj<-vulcan.normalize(vobj)
names(vobj$samples)
load(system.file("extdata","network.rda",package="vulcandata",mustWork=TRUE))
vobj_analysis<-vulcan(vobj,network=network,contrast=c("t90","t0"),minsize=5)
plot(vobj_analysis$msviper,mrs=7)

workflows.name: gsea_pareto
workflows.intent: Perform Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) with a Pareto tail distribution for p-value estimation.
input: reflist.rds (named numeric vector of gene signatures)
set.rds (character vector of gene names in the gene set)
workflows.stages: 1. Run GSEA using gsea with method="pareto" ;; 2. Plot GSEA results using plot_gsea

workflows.name: rank_enrichment_analysis
workflows.intent: Calculate enrichment of groups of gene sets over a vector of signature values using linear algebraic matrix multiplication.
input: signatures.rds (named numeric vector of gene signatures)
groups.rds (named list of character vectors representing gene sets)
